fields: (a grid block, as: "route"): h, intro, items [{t, d, draw}]. draw: the fixture at the stop (washer, analyzer, bench, humidifier, hood); without it a bench tap. Up to six stops, placed in flow order on fixed positions (top floor left and right, middle floor right and left, ground floor left and right).
best_for: BuildingLoop sets the places a central plant feeds in one building as a building section on a navy band: one pale loop leaves the plant on the ground floor, threads three floors to numbered stops, and returns under the slab; each stop is named in the margin beside it, with a numbered caption per stop under the band.

instances.h: Where water goes in a laboratory building

block.h: Where water goes in a laboratory building
block.intro: University, hospital, quality control, biotech and battery research buildings: one central plant feeds the benches.

items.d: They draw in batches, so storage is sized to carry the peak.
To the analyzer maker's specification, which governs.
ASTM D1193-24 Type II or III at bench taps, or clinical laboratory reagent water.
Fed from the loop, to the humidifier maker's specification.
Type I water from a point-of-use polisher at the bench, from its own maker. The loop feeds it to that maker's specification.
